title: A callee's effect ROW changes; its unedited cross-module callers' diagnostics and effect-row index entries change with it, and nothing else does
pins: The effect-row shape of ES-04 (roadmap-v0.13-v0.15 §4.4 gate 3, the effect-row script). combinators.calr declares a row-polymorphic Map<eff e> whose parameter row §E{e} is instantiated by two callers in app.calr — UsePure (with a pure function) and UseImpure (with a printing one) — across a module boundary; bystander.calr never calls it and is never edited. Step 1 widens Map's declared row (§E{e, alloc, mut} → §E{e, alloc, mut, cw}) so the unedited UsePure now uses 'cw' it did not declare (Calor0410 on a file that was not touched). Step 2 erases the row instead: Map loses <eff e> and its parameter's §E{e}, so invoking the row-less f inside Map is Calor0425 (cannot tell) plus the fail-closed Calor0410 on Map, and the callers' rank-1 instantiation no longer applies. THE DIAGNOSTICS LEG is what carries the stale-cache claim: a per-file cache that served the callers' effect summaries stale would let the unedited caller's Calor0410 vanish on a warm build, and the full-vs-incremental comparison catches it. THE INDEX LEG IS FRESH-VS-FRESH — ProjectIndexBuilder holds no cache, so no script in this corpus can express a STALE EffectRows facet; what ES-08 pins there is that the facet is a function of the workspace state and moves with the row edit on combinators.calr, while app.calr contributes no effrow row at all (its §C{Map} is cross-module, so it appears only under residual-effect-rows-unavailable, asserted at every step). The dedicated ES-08 delta test pins that the delta is confined to combinators.calr and app.calr while bystander.calr's diagnostics and index lines are byte-identical at every step.
reuseNote: The file set and options are constant across the three steps, so the driver's cache is exercised on the warm sequence: at least one file is served from it across the steps (the witness is aggregate, not per-file — see v0.13-freeze-registrations.md F-3′ §4 on what it can observe).
